pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/lib/utils/sanitizers/maskSensitive.ts:102 the secret-prefix vocabulary is a hand-copied regex also held at src-tauri/core/src/utils/sanitization.rs:66, src-tauri/src/main.rs:234 and src-tauri/core/src/redact.rs:52 with no parity check, so a new token class added to one copy leaks through the others

techniques.evidence: src/lib/utils/sanitizers/maskSensitive.ts:98 the comment itself records that the TS forms were copied from core/src/redact.rs after the TS copy had leaked 13 of 20 token shapes; one decision (what a secret looks like) lives in four hand-maintained encodings, the information-leakage failure
src-tauri/src/main.rs:234 the app binary builds its own copy of the redaction regex instead of going through the core redaction module, so redaction has more than one door

pairs.registryProposal: module-depth's information-leakage rule is stated for modules in one language; the commonest real case here is the same vocabulary hand-mirrored across the IPC language boundary (Rust and TS). A technique note on cross-language vocabularies (generate one from the other, or a shared fixture corpus both sides test against) would make this finding actionable instead of only diagnosable.
